- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 35.63 → 35.72+).
- Model underreacts to large true price drops (e.g., 38.18 → 34.15) — fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds high forecasts even after true prices fall sharply.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values; consider applying a downward adjustment factor based on recent volatility or low-price periods.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, then fails to correct.
- Lagged response to true price reversals — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true drop.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high prices; use rolling median or moving average to smooth out short-term noise.
